questions.stem:
The work function of a photosensitive metal is $2.1\ \mathrm{eV}$. When light of frequency $6 \times 10^{14}\ \mathrm{Hz}$ is incident on the metal surface, the maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons is:
(Take $h = 4.14 \times 10^{-15}\ \mathrm{eV\cdot s}$)
questions.solution:
According to Einstein's photoelectric equation:
$K_{\text{max}} = h\nu - \phi$
$h\nu = (4.14 \times 10^{-15}\ \mathrm{eV\cdot s}) \times (6 \times 10^{14}\ \mathrm{s}^{-1}) = 2.484\ \mathrm{eV}$.
$K_{\text{max}} = 2.484\ \mathrm{eV} - 2.1\ \mathrm{eV} = 0.384\ \mathrm{eV}$.

questions.stem: A radiation of energy $E$ falls normally on a perfectly reflecting surface. The momentum transferred to the surface is: (where $c$ is the velocity of light)
questions.solution:
For a perfectly reflecting surface, the change in momentum of each photon of energy $E_i$ is $ rac{2 E_i}{c}$.
Thus, the total momentum transferred to the surface is $ rac{2E}{c}$.
If the question asks for the coefficient of $E/c$, it is 2.

questions.stem: The work function of a substance is $3.0 \mathrm{eV}$. The longest wavelength of light that can cause photoelectric emission from this substance is $\lambda_0 = x \times 10^2 \mathrm{nm}$. The value of $x$ is: (Take $hc = 1240 \mathrm{eV\cdot nm}$, round off the value of $x$ to the nearest integer)
questions.solution:
Threshold wavelength $\lambda_0 = \frac{hc}{\phi}$.
$\lambda_0 = \frac{1240 \mathrm{eV\cdot nm}}{3.0 \mathrm{eV}} \approx 413.33 \mathrm{nm}$.
Comparing with $x \times 10^2 \mathrm{nm} = 4.1333 \times 10^2 \mathrm{nm}$.
To the nearest integer, $x = 4$.
